#6085. Mobile Passport Control: Free App That Speeds Up US Immigration

Frequent travelers to the United States are probably familiar with Global Entry, which allows enrolled members to get expedited immigration at US airports. However, applying for Global Entry is a bit of a process, and there’s a cost to participate.

If you don’t want Global Entry (or aren’t eligible), your next best option is Mobile Passport Control. This is sort of a hidden program that doesn’t get talked about enough, given that it can significantly cut down your wait times at US immigration. In this post, I’d like to talk about how this works, as I’ve used it a couple of times now (when traveling internationally with our younger son, who doesn’t yet have Global Entry).

Mobile Passport Control (MPC) is a free app that allows travelers to submit their travel document, photo, and customs declaration information, before they arrive at the immigration checkpoint at a US airport.

Travelers just have to download the app, which is available for Apple and Android. The idea is that the app streamlines the traveler’s entry process to the United States by reducing passport control inspection times and overall wait times.

Those who use MPC can access a separate immigration screening checkpoint. Really that’s the biggest advantage — because not many people use this program (as of now), the wait times are generally much shorter than the standard wait times.

There are some important things to be aware of, as you’d expect:

In the interest of being thorough, here are the current airports participating in Mobile Passport Control:

The Mobile Passport Control app couldn’t be much easier to use. I’d recommend downloading the app prior to boarding your flight to the United States, and completing the basic requirements. Then you have to submit your customs declaration after you land in the United States (within four hours of when you intend to clear immigration).

Once you download the app, there are several pages explaining how the app works, plus you have to agree to a disclaimer statement.

After that you can go through steps required for a particular entry to the country. Note that you can use one app to submit your application for multiple people in the same family. Furthermore, you can save the passport details in the app for multiple trips, eliminating the need to submit all of this information each time (though you do need to make a customs declaration each time).

To start the process, you’ll have to state which CBP port you’ll be arriving at, and they all show on a dropdown menu.

At that point you’ll have to select the travelers who will be entering the country. If you’ve already saved people to your profile, they’ll show on that page. Otherwise you can start from scratch, which just requires scanning the document, and then all the information will be auto-populated.

You’ll then need to capture traveler photos. This doesn’t need to be a passport-quality photo — you just have to follow some very basic guidelines, like removing hats and sunglasses, and making sure only one person’s face is visible.

The above can all be saved to your profile. However, what you do need to complete with each trip is answering six standard CBP declaration questions.

You’ll only want to submit this when you arrive at your point of entry in the United States. The app asks you to submit this once you’ve arrived at the airport, though in reality you have up to four hours to go through immigration from the time that your application is submitted.

Once you submit your document, you’ll be given a receipt with a QR code, which you’ll need to scan when you see an immigration officer.

Once you land at your US point of entry and arrive in the immigration hall, look for the Mobile Passport Control signage. This will bring you to an area separate from the standard US immigration line.

You still need to queue to see an immigration officer, and when you get to the officer, you’ll see a scanning device where you should scan your QR code. The benefit is that this line is usually much shorter, and also that you generally won’t be asked as many questions (since you’ve already answered some questions via the app).

Both times I’ve gone through the MPC lane, the wait was less than five minutes, while the general immigration line looked much longer. The main benefit of MPC isn’t even the time savings from getting some of the work done in advance through the app, but rather just having access to a shorter line.

Mobile Passport Control isn’t as good as Global Entry, plain and simple. With Global Entry there’s almost never a wait, you just have to look at the camera, an officer acknowledges you, and then you’re usually sent on your way. The Mobile Passport Control experience isn’t as seamless. However, it’s the next best thing.

There’s no enrollment cost, using the app takes maybe a few minutes to set up, and then with each trip it just takes a minute or so to answer the declaration questions. Getting access to a special immigration line for that is awesome, as it could potentially save you a significant amount of time.

Of course like many things in life, I imagine that as this app becomes more popular and well known, it will also become less useful. After all, when everyone gets access to a special lane, no one gets access to a special lane. 😉

Mobile Passport Control is an awesome free app that can save you time at US immigration. The app is easy to use, and allows you to submit your documents and customs declaration prior to speaking to an immigration officer. Most valuable of all, those with MPC get access to a special lane at immigration, which is typically much shorter than the standard one.

While I’d still recommend Global Entry, those who don’t have it should use MPC if they’re eligible.

Have you ever used Mobile Passport Control before? If so, what was your experience like?

#6084. Senate Dems dismiss talk of earlier leadership election; Schumer confident

Senate Minority Leader Charles E. Schumer, D-N.Y., leaves the Senate Democrats’ lunch meeting in the Capitol on Nov. 10. (Bill Clark/CQ Roll Call)

Senate Democrats moved Tuesday to squelch talk of an accelerated timeline for the vote for a new majority leader, signaling they intend to keep the contest on Dec. 1.

That the timing of the vote was already becoming a flashpoint in the caucus speaks to the rocky start for the incoming majority despite a near-sweep of key midterm races that could give Democrats 56 seats in the chamber.

The prospect of an earlier vote had been floated as a way to prevent internal divisions from hobbling the incoming majority before the 120th Congress even began.

But supporters of Sen. Chris Van Hollen, D-Md., both in the chamber and among party activists outside it, were increasingly casting the idea of a shorter contest as a bid to halt momentum for his bid against Senate Minority Leader Charles E. Schumer, D-N.Y.

Even as Schumer maintained that he has the votes necessary to be elected as majority leader, several senators insisted Tuesday the discussion taking place within the caucus was a good thing.

“I’m confident I’ll be the next leader. I have the votes,” Schumer told reporters on Tuesday following the conference’s lunch.

Van Hollen for his part told reporters Tuesday he believes his bid has “momentum at this point in time, which is why there was an effort to short-circuit the process.”

“And fortunately, I think that will fail.”

Several senators leaving the meeting said the topic of the leadership contest did not come up at all, and that neither Van Hollen nor Schumer gave a presentation regarding their bids.

That was in large part due to the absence of the incoming senators — which could be as high as 13, depending on how the dust settles in Alaska — who are able to vote in the leadership elections. Retiring senators do not cast a ballot.

With such a large class of incoming freshman, several incumbents saw it crucial to keep the election scheduled as is.

“No one has ever raised that with me. I mean, I saw a rumor that some were wanting to contemplate that,” Sen. Tim Kaine, D-Va., said Tuesday after the meeting. “The leadership discussions did not come up today. And part of the reason is we didn’t have the newcomers.”

“Remember, they all get a vote in the leadership discussion, and it would be hard to get them here,” Kaine continued, noting that only Sen.-elect Scott Colom, D-Miss., was present for Tuesday’s lunch amid his belated orientation. “But nobody else was here, and that discussion needs to have the newcomers because newcomers get votes. The outgoers don’t, right?”

Sen. Martin Heinrich, D-N.M. echoed that sentiment on Monday evening, saying, “I want to hear from the freshman class as well.”

Sen. Mazie K. Hirono, D-Hawaii, said, “I don’t know that” when asked about moving up the elections. “I think that we need to make sure that there’s enough time for what I would call a robust discussion about what we’re going to do. I think we should be very embracing of the new people who have been through fire to get here, and I think that we have to make sure that all these voices are heard.

“They’ve got a lot of talent to bring to the table,” she said.

Several senators-elect are among those who have publicly thrown their hats into Van Hollen’s corner, including Peggy Flanagan of Minnesota and Abdul El-Sayed of Michigan.El-Sayed on Tuesday said at The Atlantic Summit that he sees Van Hollen as “unique” in his experience in the Senate and running the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee as well as what he called “a willingness to take risks.”

“We need people who are willing to take legislative risk,” he said. “We need to rethink the way we legislate. It just should not be the process where you make one or two omnibus pieces of legislation that nobody really knows what’s in them,” he continued, advocating for piecemeal legislation.

But there are about 15 Democrats who have publicly backed Schumer’s bid. If former Rep. Mary Peltola maintains her lead in the lone outstanding Senate race in Alaska, Schumer would need 29 to secure the helm of the ship.

“I committed to Sen. Schumer literally months ago, and I continue to support him,” Sen. Richard Blumenthal, D-Conn., said Monday. “I’m incredibly excited about the new ideas that our new colleagues have, and their energy, and the potential for changing the way we operate in the Senate, which we have to do because we need to be more effective.”

Several incumbents have also thrown their support behind Van Hollen for leadership change, including Sens. Jeff Merkley of Oregon and Bernie Sanders of Vermont.“I think, as I’ve said many times, the American people want change in the way we do business here in Washington, and I think Chris Van Hollen would be a great leader of the Democrats,” Sanders said Monday.

Several senators and senators-elect are refusing to comment publicly on who they’ll back.

That included Sen. Ben Ray Lujan, D-N.M., who said he wants “to hear the commitments from folks that are pursuing this leadership role as well as every leadership position in the Senate, as well as chairs of committees, to what their commitments are to having a strong agenda that’s going to improve people’s lives.”

Kaine is also in that camp, and insisted Monday he hadn’t made up his mind. But he did speak positively of Schumer’s recruiting efforts in the midterms and history of dealing with a Trump White House.

“Schumer just delivered a major win for us. No one who was not on the ballot worked harder for this victory than Chuck Schumer,” he said. “Chuck Schumer also happens to know Donald Trump better than anybody else in the caucus, and dealing with this wounded president is going to be a challenge over the next few years.”

“The voters are also overwhelmingly demanding change,” he said. “So we got to figure that out as a caucus, and we’re going to be able to. And we’re not afraid to have a discussion because we’re Democrats. We like democracy.”

Sen. John Hickenlooper, D-Colo., also remained mum on who he’ll support but said, “You can’t argue” Schumer brought Democrats the majority.

“I think it’s a healthy thing to try and improve how the conference goes about its business,” he said. “I don’t think that is a distraction. We can deal with some distractions. We have to keep our eye on the ball.”

Sen. Elissa Slotkin, D-Mich., who last week called for new leadership in a news conference with Sanders, days before Van Hollen’s announcement, was noncommittal arriving to the Capitol on Monday if that meant she’d be supporting the Maryland Democrat.

Senate Democrats’ election will most likely be a secret ballot. And most senators remained unified against moving the leadership elections before they recess for the Thanksgiving break.

“They should not be moved up. There was a reason that those rule changes took place before, and they should take place in December,” Lujan said.

Kaine dismissed Van Hollen’s challenge as anything unusual.

“We’re Democrats. It’s frankly unusual that there usually [aren’t] challenges to Democratic leaders because we’re Democrats,” he said. “It’s been a little unusual to have been here for 13 years and not really have them like this. But I think it’s a discussion not just about the two contenders for the leader role, but also the leadership team and priorities, and it’s all wrapped up in one discussion.”

“That’s why we decided, don’t do these votes until December, because you want to let the election settle and understand exactly what’s up, and then hear from potential votes.”

Sen. Andy Kim, D-N.J., said, “I think we should stick with the rules when it comes to the caucus. … That’s going to be what makes sure that we show that we have a real process.”

Sanders asked: “Why would anyone want to do that?” when asked.

“I think there’s a date that’s been called, and that should be the date.”

#6082. Chase Ink Business Unlimited Bonus: 75K Points Welcome Offer

The Ink Business Unlimited® Credit Card is part of the Chase Ink Business card portfolio, and is one of the best no annual fee cards out there. It’s one of the rewarding Chase cards for everyday spending, and a great complement to some of Chase’s more premium cards.

In this post, I’d like to take a look at the Chase Ink Business Unlimited bonus, as it’s one of the best welcome offers you’ll find on any no annual fee card.

Link: Learn more about the Ink Business Unlimited® Credit Card with 75K bonus points

The Chase Ink Unlimited Card is offering a welcome bonus of 75,000 points after spending $6,000 within the first three months. You’ll see the Ink Unlimited bonus is marketed as offering cash back, rather than points, so it’s described as being worth $750. Indeed, you could redeem the rewards as cash back.

However, if you have the card in conjunction with a card earning Ultimate Rewards points, like the Chase Sapphire Reserve® Card (learn more) or Sapphire Reserve for Business℠ (learn more), then rewards can be transferred to Ultimate Rewards airline and hotel partners.

Based on my latest miles & points valuations, I consider Ultimate Rewards points to be worth 1.7 cents each, and that increases the value of the points by 70% right there, as far as I’m concerned. I consider the 75,000 points to be worth $1,275. That’s a great bonus, especially for a no annual fee card.

With the ability to transfer Chase points to partners at a 1:1 ratio, that opens up all kinds of great redemption opportunities, including:

How does the Chase Ink Unlimited 75,000-point offer compare to past publicly available bonuses that we’ve seen on the card? Below is a chart with the Chase Ink Unlimited welcome offer history in recent years.

As you can see, the Chase Ink Unlimited publicly available welcome offer typically ranges from 75,000 to 100,000 points. The offer of 75,000 points is excellent, but is the standard offer. If you are willing to wait, we might see another offer of 90,000 points, or a return of the best-ever offer of 100,000 points.

However, the offer of 75,000 points is still great, and I’d decide whether to apply now or wait based on how much value you’d get from the card in the coming months. For a no annual fee card, the offer of 75,000 points is still industry leading.

When it comes to getting approved for the Chase Ink Unlimited Card and earning the welcome bonus, what rules should you be aware of? Well, there are the card specific policies, and then also the more generic Chase policies. When you pull up the application, you’ll see the following terms:

The new cardmember bonus may not be available to you if you have ever had this card or any other Chase for Business card without an annual fee. We may also consider factors pertinent to your business in determining your bonus eligibility.

As you can see, officially the Ink Unlimited bonus isn’t available to you if you’ve had this exact card, or another Chase business card without an annual fee, including the Ink Business Cash® Credit Card (learn more). So there is an element of cards being mutually exclusive.

However, the key here is that you “may” not be eligible, and not that you absolutely won’t be eligible. I don’t love that level of vagueness, though the good news is that if you apply for the card and aren’t eligible for the bonus, you should receive a pop-up message informing you of this, before there’s a hard pull. So that at least means the downside of applying is limited.

The good news is that eligibility for the bonus is completely unrelated to whether you have a Chase business card with an annual fee, like the Ink Business Preferred® Credit Card (learn more) or Sapphire Reserve for Business℠ (learn more).

It’s fine to apply for Chase business cards as a sole proprietorship, corporation, etc. If you apply as a sole proprietorship, you can just enter your Social Security Number in the section where you’d otherwise put your EIN.

Beyond that, there are some general Chase rules to be aware of:

There’s not a consistent credit score you need to get approved for the Chase Ink Unlimited, though I’d hope to have a score in the “good” to “excellent” range, ideally 700+ points. However, people with lower scores have been approved, and people with higher scores have been rejected, as it’s one of only many factors that impacts card eligibility.

The Chase Ink Unlimited Card has no annual fee, and there are several reasons to consider picking it up. The way I view it, there are a few points that are most important.

For one, the card has a solid rewards structure, as it offers a minimum of 1.5x points on all spending, making it one of the best Chase cards for everyday spending (the card does have foreign transaction fees, though, so I’d only recommend using it for US purchases). Furthermore, the card offers primary rental car coverage, which can come in handy if you rent cars with any frequency, and is incredibly rare for a no annual fee card.

Also, since the card has no annual fee, there’s really no opportunity cost to holding onto it, and it allows you to create a great portfolio of cards to maximize rewards.

Read my review of the Chase Ink Unlimited Card.

The Chase Ink Unlimited Card is one of the most lucrative no annual fee cards out there, and it’s currently offering a welcome bonus of 75,000 points upon completing minimum spending.

Not only does the card have a great bonus that’s too good to turn down, but it offers rewards that can make it worth holding onto, like 1.5x points on everyday spending, plus rental car coverage. If you’re eligible for this card, I think there’s a lot of merit to picking it up. Taking advantage of this bonus is a no-brainer, if eligible.

Do you have the Chase Ink Unlimited Card, and if so, what has your experience been?

#6080. Mary Peltola unseats Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan in Alaska

Former Alaska Rep. Mary Peltola speaks during her election night party in Anchorage on Nov. 3. (Charly Triballeau/ AFP via Getty Images)

Former Rep. Mary Peltola has defeated Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan in Alaska, giving Senate Democrats their ninth pickup of the midterm elections and bringing their caucus’s total seats in the next Congress to 56.

The Associated Press called the race for Peltola around 10:19 p.m. Eastern time on Tuesday, a full two weeks after Election Day. The latest tranche of ballots counted put the former congresswoman past the 50-percent threshold to win the election outright without Alaska’s ranked choice voting system kicking in.

With her victory, Peltola, who is Yup’ik, becomes one of the first Native American women elected to the Senate, along with fellow Democrat Peggy Flanagan, who won the open seat in Minnesota this month.

“As a lifelong Alaskan who has dedicated my life to serving our state, there is no greater honor than having Alaskans’ support in our fight to take on corporate greed, lower costs, and put Alaska first.,” Peltola said in a statement after the race was called.

The Alaska race was the final Senate contest to be called in a midterm election that saw Democrats win commanding majorities in both chambers of Congress. Besides Alaska, Democrats also flipped Senate seats in North Carolina, Maine, Ohio, Texas, Iowa, Kansas, South Carolina and Mississippi.

Peltola, a former state legislator, made history in 2022 when she became the first Alaska Native elected to Congress, winning a special election for the state’s at-large district. She comfortably won the general election that fall but was narrowly unseated in 2024 by Republican Nick Begich.

She entered the Senate contest in January, positioning herself as an independent-minded Democrat and invoking the legacies of two well-liked Alaska Republicans, the late Sen. Ted Stevens and the late Rep. Don Young, whom she succeeded in the House.

She campaigned on the slogan “fish, family, freedom” and played up her moderate views and deep roots in the state.

But the race was marked by allegations of political gamesmanship. In addition to the incumbent Sullivan, a retired colonel in the U.S. Marine Corps Reserves, the Senate ballot also included a retired teacher named Dan J. Sullivan. The New York Times reported late last month that operatives aligned with Peltola’s campaign were involved in the effort to recruit the second Dan Sullivan in an attempt to confuse voters.

Peltola has said she had no connection to the scheme.

Prior to Election Day, the Trump administration filed a lawsuit seeking to delay certification of the result if Sen. Sullivan were to lose. The lawsuit was tossed earlier this month by a federal judge.

Trump also suggested that all votes cast for Dan J. Sullivan should be added to the incumbent’s total. “If you add them up, Dan Sullivan wins,” the president told reporters Monday. But as of Tuesday evening when the race was called, Peltola had more votes than both Sullivans combined.

The Alaska race was initially viewed as a long shot for Democrats. The Last Frontier has elected a Democratic senator just once in the past 50 years – in 2008, when Mark Begich ousted Stevens. Begich, the Democratic uncle of the current Republican congressman, served a single term before he was ousted by Sullivan in 2014.

But anger in Alaska over the rising cost of food and fuel — already among the highest in the nation — provided Democrats with an opening.

"56 seats was an unimaginable result even just a few months ago," Senate Democratic leader Charles E. Schumer said in a statement Tuesday night. "But I knew if we concentrated on getting the best candidates, and if we focused like a laser on the costs, corruption, and chaos that Donald Trump has wrought throughout America, we would have shot."

In other Alaska races, Democrats flipped the governor’s mansion, with former state Rep. Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins winning an open-seat race to become the first Democrat elected governor of the state since Tony Knowles won a second term in 1998.

The race for the state’s at-large House district will be decided by ranked choice voting, with tabulations expected to take place Wednesday. Begich, the GOP incumbent, was leading Tuesday with 47.5 percent of the vote and is expected to prevail over independent Bill Hill, who had the backing of national Democrats and trailed with 42 percent. Another Democrat and a Libertarian combined for the remainder of the vote.

If you're not yet a member, you can score 1,500 bonus miles when you join Rove through TPG's link and an additional 5,000 bonus miles on your first hotel booking over $500 with code "BRIANKELLY500."

Priceline's vast menu of Black Friday travel deals — on flights, car rentals, vacation packages, cruises and more — includes hotels as well. Travelers can score up to 40% at select hotels, with the most savings on stays of two nights or more. Plus, you can save $100 on select Disney destination hotels with code "DISNEYBF100."

Members of Priceline's VIP loyalty program (it's free to join) get access to the above deals starting Nov. 16, and the sale opens to nonmembers on Nov. 23. It will run through Dec. 2 at 9 a.m. Eastern.

Priceline will also be dropping limited-time flash sales for Black Friday, Cyber Monday, and Travel Tuesday:

As with Priceline, the One Key loyalty family — Expedia, Hotels.com and Vrbo — has a slew of travel deals coming up for Black Friday, Cyber Monday and Travel Tuesday. Among them, you’ll find rates slashed up to 50% at thousands of hotels and vacation rentals.

Even better, these deals are valid for travel through Dec. 30, 2027, giving you plenty of time to plan.

Hotels.com has also teased a special coupon for an extra 15% off, set to drop on Cyber Monday.

If you'd like to give the gift of travel, consider buying a Hotels.com gift card this holiday season. You can save 10% on gift cards of $100-plus and 15% on $300-plus from Nov. 23 through Dec. 31.

Is a vacation rental more your style? At Vrbo, travelers can save hundreds of dollars when booking a vacation rental 60 days in advance. Use the Early Booking and Weekly Stay discount filters to search for deals.

You can also expect special flash deals of up to 75% off select stays. These will go live at 9 a.m. ET on Black Friday, Cyber Monday and Travel Tuesday — but act fast, because quantities are limited.

If Vegas is on your wish list this year, you won’t want to miss this sale.

MGM is offering up to 30% off room rates at various Las Vegas properties, including Bellagio Las Vegas, Park MGM Las Vegas, and Aria Resort & Casino. Book by Dec. 3 at noon Eastern time with offer code "TLTMSTN."

Cyber Monday and Travel Tuesday are some of the best days of the year to plan vacations. Major hotel brands offer significant savings on stays you actually want to book, making the deals even sweeter. But don’t sleep on these deals: While the booking window may seem generous, it goes by fast.

#6076. Your Flight Takes 10 Minutes Longer Than It Used To—And That’s A Luxury Worth Paying For

Flying takes longer than it used to – and, retirement of the Concorde notwithstanding, it’s not because planes aren’t as fast. There are more than twice as many commercial flights as there were at the time of airline deregulation, and air traffic control hasn’t been upgraded very much. There’s congested airspace and also congested airports. We also don’t build major new airports – the last one was Denver, 30 years ago. (Austin’s new 1999 airport was a converted military base, and there were others like that in the 90s.) By one estimate flights have gotten 8% longer. That means a two hour flight is 10 minutes longer than it used to be. And the single biggest factor is often tagged as strategic padding of schedules. Airlines are often chided for ‘schedule padding’ – claiming that flights take longer than they should. Often, this just reflects the reality of telling customers when they can expect to arrive – although there’s greater variance than there used to be, which isn’t great for having a gate available when you land early. Airlines do not like this! Though real airfares (even including fees) are down significantly since deregulation, longer flight times are expensive for staffing, fuel and efficient use of $50 – $100 million planes. And longer travel times historically disadvantaged an airline trying to sell tickets, because it meant their flights were displayed lower on the screen that travel agents and later passengers directly saw – which translates into fewer sales. A new study finds that airlines with more “padding” in their schedules tend to charge higher fares. That sounds like passengers paying more for a slower trip. But those extra minutes can also let United hold your plane with ConnectionSaver and get you home that night, and still arrive on time. It also means fewer delays and missed connections. So that ‘premium’ is actually a more valuable product to many consumers. I’ve argued for years that schedule padding often isn’t really padding. Sometimes an airline is finally admitting how long the trip takes. Customers can plan around an honest arrival time. There’s a new chapter by Embry-Riddle’s Jules Yimga, “The Price of Punctuality,” in The Economics of Airline Pricing. It combines 2019 flight time data with the government’s ticket price survey. It compares schedules against different percentiles of actual flight times, then examines how the resulting measures relate to fares. More padding is associated with higher fares, especially when the comparison uses the faster end of actual flight times. The relationship appears in both competitive and concentrated markets. The abstract itself allows that reliability could be a service customers value. (Interestingly, Yimga’s earlier research on schedule padding attributed higher prices primarily to higher costs rather than higher margins.) Even scheduling to the median arrival time means roughly half of trips take longer than published. It’s often better for a customer if an airline underpromises and overdelivers – or arrives ‘on time’ rather than late. Predictability matters when you’re scheduling connections or trying to arrive in time for a meeting. An airline that leaves little buffer is going to appear less reliable, so customers book earlier flights and longer layovers or even fly in the night before an important meeting. Then the buffer hasn’t disappeared, it just changes who’s scheduling it. That’s why I argued American’s investment in more realistic schedules could pay for itself. Avoiding rebooking, mishandled bags and aircraft and crews getting out of position can justify spending running an on-time schedule even before a customer chooses the airline again because the trip met expectations. American’s Dallas – Fort Worth overhaul that began in April combined longer scheduled flight times with a move from nine daily banks of flights to thirteen. Spreading flights into smaller waves reduced congestion that made some of the extra time unnecessary. One plane waiting for a gate can delay its passengers, its next departure, and other flights whose crews are stuck on board. Giving the operation room to recover can prevent that problem from cascading. In January, I covered American network planning chief Brian Znotins explaining that bookings for 40–54 minute connections at DFW were 4% below what its model predicted. Bookings for 55–84 minute connections were 8% above prediction. Customers have actually started choosing longer connections because they feel more reliable and less likely to leave them stranded. When I covered United’s media day in 2019, Greg Hart explained that 25% of its flights each day were expected to arrive ten minutes early. That gave United room to use ConnectionSaver to hold flights for connecting passengers and still arrive on time. Of course there’s such a thing as too much slack. An airline can improve its reported punctuality by moving the promised arrival later without getting anyone anywhere sooner. Excessively long connections waste customer time. And routinely beating an absurdly generous schedule doesn’t make an operation excellent. Not all padding is something customers will pay a premium for. I disagree. 2 hour flights with a 2:45 min scheduled flight time does no one any good except airline on time performance. Each airport has a minimum connection time so connections are not pushed. You can not even book close connections on airline sites unless it’s 2 individual flights or you mix carriers. Airline connections get sloppier and sloppier and playing with the numbers just makes connecting flights a poorer choice. Airlines should be honest and live with the consequences of their gate and operations failures. Extrapolated to the extreme you will schedule 2 hours of flying over 4 hours once you pad both flights and the actual connection time.

>Sometimes an airline is finally admitting how long the trip takes.

@paul agree on connections. Pad both legs while the minimum connection time stays the same and a tight connection looks fine on paper, then you’re sprinting through DFW. 2 hours on a domestic connection is a sane buffer IMO

Delta has always padded their flight times to keep their on-time rating high.

This isn’t exactly news but I’m surprised more airlines didn’t think of this sooner so they can come up with bogus marketing slogans like “#1 airline in the US”

Flight time should be based on actual data not a theoretical time it would take. So I’m good with this practice.

#6075. Hilton’s Cyber Week Bonus Is Worth Just $8—But You Can Stack Three Offers For 10,000 Points On A Single Night

Hilton Honors will give you 2,000 bonus points per stay if you book by Tuesday, December 1. I value Hilton points at 0.4 cents apiece. That’s $8 for a night at a Hampton Inn or $8 for a week at a Conrad. Book directly with Hilton. The booking window opened November 24, 2026, for stays completed November 25, 2026 through April 2, 2027. There’s no registration required or cap. (Hat tip to Head for Points.) For stays through December 31, 2026, register for More Points to Play before checkout. It adds 1,000 points at most hotels or 3,000 at listed luxury, lifestyle, resort and all-inclusive properties. With both offers that’s 3,000 points ($12) or 5,000 ($20). Award stays qualify for the fall offer. Hilton’s Cyber Week terms aren’t explicit on this but don’t exclude them. Book a Hilton Sale rate and pay the whole bill with a U.S. Hilton American Express card and you can earn another 5,000 points once per cardholder (book by December 22, stay by April 2). Book by December 1 and check out by December 31 to combine all three offers. That’s 8,000 bonus points ($32) at most hotels. At a property on the higher bonus list, one night can earn 10,000 bonus points ($40) before you count the usual hotel and card earnings. In the U.S. and Canada, the sale rate takes up to 20% off Hilton’s best available rate and requires booking at least seven days ahead. At most Hilton and Marriott brands, $100 in eligible room charges earns 1,000 base points. That’s $4 back at Hilton against about $6 at Marriott. Back in 2010, Hilton’s Jeff Diskin explained that Hilton got too little credit for what it gave every member and so promotions let them drive business. For years Hilton offered double points almost all the time. That lifted the return at most brands from 4% to 8% before elite or card bonuses. This year two months went by between the summer offer ending August 15 and the fall one starting October 15. Hilton seems to run promotions less frequently than they used to, but promotions are core to the program’s earning proposition being competitive. It’s worth repricing refundable Hilton stays booked before November 24. The fall offer already covers existing reservations, so it’s the Cyber Week add-on that’s worth considering (I wouldn’t bother rebooking if the room rate has gone up). Book directly with Hilton. The booking window opened November 24, 2026, for stays completed November 25, 2026 through April 2, 2027. There’s no registration required or cap. (Hat tip to Head for Points.)

For stays through December 31, 2026, register for More Points to Play before checkout. It adds 1,000 points at most hotels or 3,000 at listed luxury, lifestyle, resort and all-inclusive properties. With both offers that’s 3,000 points ($12) or 5,000 ($20). Award stays qualify for the fall offer. Hilton’s Cyber Week terms aren’t explicit on this but don’t exclude them.

Book a Hilton Sale rate and pay the whole bill with a U.S. Hilton American Express card and you can earn another 5,000 points once per cardholder (book by December 22, stay by April 2). Book by December 1 and check out by December 31 to combine all three offers. That’s 8,000 bonus points ($32) at most hotels. At a property on the higher bonus list, one night can earn 10,000 bonus points ($40) before you count the usual hotel and card earnings.

In the U.S. and Canada, the sale rate takes up to 20% off Hilton’s best available rate and requires booking at least seven days ahead.

At most Hilton and Marriott brands, $100 in eligible room charges earns 1,000 base points. That’s $4 back at Hilton against about $6 at Marriott. Back in 2010, Hilton’s Jeff Diskin explained that Hilton got too little credit for what it gave every member and so promotions let them drive business.

For years Hilton offered double points almost all the time. That lifted the return at most brands from 4% to 8% before elite or card bonuses. This year two months went by between the summer offer ending August 15 and the fall one starting October 15. Hilton seems to run promotions less frequently than they used to, but promotions are core to the program’s earning proposition being competitive.

It’s worth repricing refundable Hilton stays booked before November 24. The fall offer already covers existing reservations, so it’s the Cyber Week add-on that’s worth considering (I wouldn’t bother rebooking if the room rate has gone up).

Small Business Saturday can bring the kind of rush every owner wants. Orders roll in, and sales climb.

But for many companies, that influx of orders can also mean an influx of bills. Extra costs for inventory, shipping or temporary help can all add up.

This year's Small Business Saturday falls on Nov. 28.

Whether you're stocking up on inventory, investing in advertising or preparing to fulfill a surge in orders, the right business card could turn those related expenses into a welcome bonus or a stronger return. It can also bridge the gap between paying suppliers and receiving your sales proceeds.

Here are eight business credit cards worth considering, depending on your spending habits, cash flow and rewards goals.

Apply for : Find out your offer and see if you are eligible for as high as 300,000 bonus points after spending $20,000 on purchases in the first three months of card membership. Welcome offers vary, and you may not be eligible for an offer.

Instant access: Eligible applicants can receive an instant card number and add it to a digital wallet after approval.

Current welcome offer: Find out your offer and see if you're eligible for as high as 200,000 Membership Rewards points after spending $15,000 on purchases in the first three months of card membership. Welcome offers vary, and you may not be eligible for an offer.

The maximum welcome bonus is worth $4,000, based on TPG's November 2026 valuations.

The is strongest when your expenses are concentrated, not scattered. It automatically earns 4 points per dollar spent in your top two eligible categories each billing cycle, on up to $150,000 in combined purchases each calendar year (then 1 point per dollar spent). Your spending picks the bonus categories, not the other way around.

That can work well around Small Business Saturday, when a surge in orders may push more of your spending into just a few purchase types. The six eligible categories are select U.S. advertising; U.S. electronic-goods retailers and software and cloud-system providers; U.S. restaurants; U.S. gas stations; transit; and U.S. wireless service.

After enrollment, you can receive up to $20 in statement credits each month on eligible U.S. purchases at Grubhub and office supply stores and on shipments at UPS.com, for up to $240 per calendar year. That could help offset some of your last-minute office supply or shipping expenses.

Learn more in our full review of the Amex Business Gold.

Instant access: Eligible applicants can receive an instant card number and add it to a digital wallet.

Current welcome offer: Find out your offer and see if you are eligible for as high as 300,000 bonus points after spending $20,000 on purchases in the first three months of card membership. Welcome offers vary, and you may not be eligible for an offer.

The can be particularly valuable for businesses making large purchases or facing significant operating expenses during the holiday season.

It earns 2 points per dollar spent on eligible U.S. purchases from shipping providers*, electronics retailers, software and cloud providers and construction-material or hardware suppliers. Individual purchases of $5,000 or more also earn 2 points per dollar spent (up to $2 million in eligible purchases each calendar year, then 1 point per dollar spent).

*Effective Feb. 17, 2027, select merchants only.

If the rush calls for new laptops, software or seasonal hires, statement credits can offset eligible purchases: cardholders can receive up to $150 in annual statement credits on U.S. Dell purchases plus $1,000 after spending $5,000 or more with Dell each calendar year, a statement credit of up to $300 a year on ChatGPT Business (subject to auto-renewal) and up to $90 in statement credits per quarter on U.S. Indeed purchases. Enrollment is required for select benefits.

I would choose this card if you expect heavy shipping, technology upgrades or major restocking invoices year-round. One successful weekend alone does not justify an $895 card.

Learn more in our full review of the Amex Business Platinum.

Instant access: Approved businesses may receive immediate access to a virtual card number.

Annual fee: $150, refunded each year you spend at least $150,000

Current welcome offer: Earn a $2,000 cash bonus after spending $30,000 on purchases in the first three months after account opening. You can also earn another $2,000 for every $500,000 spent during your first year.

The Spark Cash Plus is the anti-spreadsheet card. It earns 2% cash back on every purchase, whether the charge is for inventory, contractors or a rush order of packing supplies because you underestimated how much tape shipping requires.

Spend $20,000 across it all and you will earn $400 cash back without tracking which purchases fall into a bonus category.

The card has no preset spending limit, although that doesn't mean you can spend an unlimited amount.

It's best for established businesses with high expenses that want cash rather than travel rewards. If your annual spending will clear $150,000, the annual-fee refund makes the decision easier.

Learn more in our full review of the Spark Cash Plus.

Instant access: Approved applicants may receive a virtual card number before the physical card arrives.

Current welcome offer: Earn 100,000 bonus miles after spending $10,000 on purchases in the first three months after account opening.

That's $1,850 in potential travel value, based on TPG's November 2026 valuations.

The Venture Business is a good default option for businesses with expenses that span multiple spending categories. It earns an unlimited 2 miles per dollar spent on every purchase, so inventory, packaging, software and freelance help all receive the same return.

Cardholders also receive a $50 annual Capital One Business Travel credit and up to $50 in annual statement credits for qualifying advertising or software purchases.

Its earning rates will not top every specialized bonus category, but it rewards the entire expense pile consistently. It is difficult to mess up, the annual fee is reasonable and the spending requirement is attainable for many businesses expecting a strong holiday season.

Choose it when you want transferable miles and simple earning without paying for a premium card.

Learn more in our full review of the Capital One Venture Business.

Instant access: Capital One may provide an immediately usable virtual card number after approval.

If you meet both spending thresholds, the full offer is worth up to $6,550 per TPG's valuations, including the $1,000 travel credit.

The Venture X Business is built for companies with substantial spending and enough cash flow to pay the bill on schedule.

The full welcome offer shouldn't be treated as a challenge, but rather as a major incentive for companies that already expect six figures of near-term expenses and can use the travel benefits afterward.

The card is designed to be paid in full, so the card only makes sense if you expect your cash flow to more or less match your purchasing volume.

The Venture X Business includes a $300 annual Capital One Business Travel credit, 10,000 anniversary miles and airport lounge access.

For business owners that will use the travel benefits, the Venture X Business can be a spectacular value with an annual fee that easily justifies itself. For companies without regular travel on the books, the Capital One Venture Business earns the same two miles per dollar spent on everyday purchases with a lower annual fee.

Learn more in our full review of the Venture X Business.

Learn more: Capital One Venture X Business

Instant access: Don't count on being able to use your card immediately after approval.

Current welcome offer: Earn 200,000 bonus points after spending $30,000 on purchases in the first six months after account opening.

That's $4,100 in potential travel value, based on TPG's November 2026 valuations.

The is excellent at one particular Small Business Saturday expense: buying more customers.

It earns 3 points per dollar spent on the first $1 million of social media and search-engine advertising each account anniversary year, then 1 point per dollar. Inventory, shipping and most other business expenses earn just 1 point per dollar.

The Sapphire Reserve for Business also offers up to $400 in statement credits annually for ZipRecruiter through Dec. 31, 2027 and up to $200 in statement credits annually for Google Workspace, plus a $300 annual travel credit and airport lounge access. That gives the card value beyond advertising for owners who already spend on software, recruiting and travel.

Choose it when paid search and social media are major expenses beyond the holiday rush, or when the business and travel perks fit within the costs you already have. Given its $795 annual fee, it's best suited to business owners who can take advantage of multiple benefits throughout the year.

Learn more in our full review of the Sapphire Reserve for Business.

Instant access: Don't count on being able to use your card immediately after approval.

Current welcome offer: Earn 100,000 bonus points after spending $8,000 on purchases within the first three months after account opening.

That's $2,050 in potential travel value, based on TPG's valuations.

The may be the cleanest match for online retailers preparing for an influx of holiday orders.

It earns 3 points per dollar spent on the first $150,000 in combined spending each account anniversary year on shipping, social media and search-engine advertising, internet, cable and phone services and travel, then 1 point per dollar.

Shipping is the obvious Small Business Saturday fit, but for online sellers focused on shipping and ads, it's the best value here. It rewards both the advertising that brings shoppers in and the shipping that gets their orders out, with a manageable annual fee.

Learn more in our full review of the Ink Business Preferred.

Small Business Saturday is a shopping holiday for customers. For owners, it's an opportunity to grow sales — but it can also bring significant operating expenses.

Whether you're investing in advertising, replenishing inventory or shipping orders to customers, the right business credit card can help you turn those expenses into valuable cash back, points or miles.

Look for a card that rewards the expenses you already incur and fits your cash flow needs. Instant access can also help if you have holiday bills to cover right away, while earning rates and other card benefits will sustain you long after Small Business Saturday is over.

Related: How to choose the right credit card for your business expenses

#6073. Turkish Airlines Looks Up Rules For The Wrong Georgia — Passenger Loses A Week And $5,000

Turkish Airlines seems to have looked up the wrong Georgia when a passenger checked in, and came up with the wrong rules for travel. A Georgian journalist and his partner were flying from Washington Dulles via Istanbul to visit family in the country next door to Turkey. He says the airline turned them away over a “Swine and Bird Import Permit” for their two pet parakeets. That’s a permit you can get in Atlanta. The airline that holds the Guinness World Record for flying to the most countries flies to both Georgias. From Istanbul they’ll take you to Atlanta or to Tbilisi or Batumi. Turkish Airlines Boeing 777 approaching Washington Dulles in 2025, credit Acroterion The state of Georgia calls its form “Swine and Bird Travel Permit Registration.” The application asks for the destination state and ZIP code. Meanwhile, the Georgian consulate’s instructions for pet birds have identification and animal health requirements but not this kind of permit. Here’s their advice on taking pets to the country of Georgia. David Nikuradze shared his story with me about his August 14 flight. After more than 20 years covering Washington for Georgian television, he and his partner were moving to Portugal. They’d spent six months preparing, met with the manager of Turkish Airlines’ Washington office and made multiple visits to the vet. They showed up with six suitcases, two budgies and a health certificate endorsed by the U.S. Department of Agriculture. But Turkish told him to just leave the birds behind. That’s also what an 81-year-old woman says Frontier told her in Puerto Rico, after they’d flown her there with her parrot, Plucky. Washington Dulles, Credit David Benbennick Nikuradze says he brought stamped letters from the Georgian authorities back to the counter the next day confirming the birds didn’t need the permit. He still couldn’t get out for a week. Turkish told him earlier flights already had cats booked. Turksih allows parakeets in the cabin but not at the same time there’s also cats and on the same plane even in different cabins. They flew August 21 on their original veterinary paperwork. But first they had to pay Turkish to rebook, finnd a pet-friendly hotel in Manassas, rent a vehicle big enough for their luggage and buy a cage so the birds could get out of their carrier. Nikuradze puts the cost at more than $5,000. Two pet budgerigars on a cage, credit Anna Saccheri Turkish Airlines check-in staff seemed to think these passegners were flying Washington D.C. to Atlanta connecting through Istanbul, which is something only Eric Adams would do. Turkish has used dnata to check in passengers and verify their documents at Dulles. Outsourcing may have played a role here. I once wrote about Turkish Airlines sending a couple to Dhaka, Bangladesh, when they’d asked for Dakar, Senegal. When the flight attendant announced Dhaka, they figured that was how you said Dakar with a Turkish accent. Turkish eventually admitted its booking agent had entered the wrong airport code and offered them two tickets anywhere it flew. For Nikuradze, I’d start by refunding the difference in airfare they paid. Meanwhile, the Georgian consulate’s instructions for pet birds have identification and animal health requirements but not this kind of permit. Here’s their advice on taking pets to the country of Georgia.

David Nikuradze shared his story with me about his August 14 flight. After more than 20 years covering Washington for Georgian television, he and his partner were moving to Portugal. They’d spent six months preparing, met with the manager of Turkish Airlines’ Washington office and made multiple visits to the vet. They showed up with six suitcases, two budgies and a health certificate endorsed by the U.S. Department of Agriculture. But Turkish told him to just leave the birds behind. That’s also what an 81-year-old woman says Frontier told her in Puerto Rico, after they’d flown her there with her parrot, Plucky.

Washington Dulles, Credit David Benbennick

Nikuradze says he brought stamped letters from the Georgian authorities back to the counter the next day confirming the birds didn’t need the permit. He still couldn’t get out for a week. Turkish told him earlier flights already had cats booked. Turksih allows parakeets in the cabin but not at the same time there’s also cats and on the same plane even in different cabins.

They flew August 21 on their original veterinary paperwork. But first they had to pay Turkish to rebook, finnd a pet-friendly hotel in Manassas, rent a vehicle big enough for their luggage and buy a cage so the birds could get out of their carrier. Nikuradze puts the cost at more than $5,000.

Turkish Airlines check-in staff seemed to think these passegners were flying Washington D.C. to Atlanta connecting through Istanbul, which is something only Eric Adams would do.

Turkish has used dnata to check in passengers and verify their documents at Dulles. Outsourcing may have played a role here.

#6072. Senator Grassley Should Heed His Own Warning

Were the longtime Iowa senator to leave office before January, the outgoing governor, Republican Kim Reynolds, would be able to appoint his successor.

Senator Chuck Grassley (R., Iowa) listens as U.S. Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem testifies before a Senate Judiciary Committee hearing on “Oversight of the Department of Homeland Security” on Capitol Hill in Washington, D.C., March 3, 2026.

Iowa Senator Chuck Grassley is the oldest member of Congress at age 93, but he remains sharp and focused.

This month, his office announced that he will not be retiring from the Senate, even though a Democrat will take office as governor in January and have the power to appoint someone if any of the state’s two U.S. Senate seats fall vacant.

John Fund is National Review’s national-affairs reporter.

#6071. American Airlines And Citi Test A $695 Business Card That Could Earn 50% More Miles And Loyalty Points

I receive compensation for content and many links on this blog. Be aware that websites may earn compensation when a customer clicks on a link, when an application is approved, or when an account is opened. Citibank is an advertising partner of this site, as is American Express, Chase, Capital One, and others. Any opinions expressed in this post are my own, and have not been reviewed, approved, or endorsed by my advertising partners. I do not write about all offers that are available -- instead focusing on miles, points, and cash back (and currencies that can be converted into the same). Terms apply to the offers and benefits listed on this page.

American Airlines and Citi are working on a $695 AAdvantage Executive card for small businesses. It’s been an odd omission. The $695 United Club Business Card already earns 1.5 miles per dollar on everyday spending. Delta Air Lines has its $650 SkyMiles Reserve Business card. American’s Admirals Club card has been a consumer product.

Doctor of Credit shares some card designs that Citi is surveying. One looks a lot like the consumer Citi® / AAdvantage® Executive World Legend Mastercard® [See rates and fees] I’ve carried for a long time. However, the other would earn: 1.5 miles and 1.5 Loyalty Points per dollar on everyday purchases. Put $100,000 of bills on one employee’s card in a qualification year and the business would earn 150,000 redeemable miles. The employee would earn 150,000 Loyalty Points, enough for Platinum Pro, and the owner would earn 100,000 Loyalty Points, enough for Platinum. In January I wrote about Citi testing a $150 fee for the regular business card and the idea of replacing its $99 companion certificate with a flight discount. Citi went ahead with the fee and kept the certificate. So not everything being tested happens, and I’d put the strongest prediction on a card like this coming at a $695 annual fee with Admirals Club membership, realizing that the rest are potential options under consideration (and in some cases even controls that aren’t going to make the final product). Credit: Doctor of Credit What The Lounge Membership Gets A Business Both versions give the primary cardmember Admirals Club membership with up to two guests. The personal card also admits immediate family, which matters when there are four (or more) of you. Employee cards carry no additional annual fee. The company can buy lounge access for the people who travel, at $175 total for the first three and $175 apiece after that. So that’s basically the same as the consumer card, except that the annual fee plus lounge is optional rather. American charges $1,200 to $1,400 for full membership, depending on status. And the clubs are getting better. I prefer the newer American lounges to what United and Delta are building. My home club in Austin is slated to double in size and get an outdoor terrace. Someone who wants the lounge may already have gotten the Citi® / AAdvantage® Executive World Legend Mastercard®. But Citi’s going to want the smaller group of customers who want big company expenses on a business account. Some Ideas Being Surveyed For The Card Both versions shared from this survey would earn 4 miles per dollar on American Airlines and 12 on eligible hotel and car bookings through American. Both come with Group 4 boarding, priority check-in and screening, Omni Champion and Avis President’s Club status, up to $100 for inflight or club purchases, and $15 in Lyft credit after three eligible rides in a month. One largely copies the personal Executive card. It earns one mile and one Loyalty Point per dollar on ordinary spending, plus 10,000 Loyalty Points at each of four balances (50,000, 90,000, 165,000 and 240,000). The other awards 1.5 Loyalty Points on every eligible dollar the cardholder spends. It drops the four milestones, along with the two $250 American Airlines Vacations credits and two $100 inKind dining credits. Instead there’s $20 a month toward Melio or Xero and half off an annual Fox One and Wall Street Journal bundle (meh). It adds Sixt to the $120 Avis and Budget credit and covers a second domestic checked bag. But its two Omni free nights interest me. On the personal Executive card you enroll and complete a qualifying stay of at least two consecutive nights booked directly with Omni to earn one free night. If this didn’t require a stay to earn that would be exceptionally valuable (I’d probably redeem them in New York or worst case if I didn’t otherwise use them, down the street at Barton Creek Resort in Austin). I like the potential add-on of rewards for $100,000 in spending, since the consumer version doesn’t really give a strong incentive to actually spend money on the card (it’s a great one to get and keep, but spending is really only incentivized by the Loyalty Points). Here they’re surveying a choice of 2,500 Loyalty Points, two Flagship Lounge passes or a $200 flight discount. American sells the passes for $150 apiece, though I’d value them as an upgrade from the Admirals Club I can already visit. It’s probably best to just take the flight discount unless the points pushed someone over a status or reward threshold. The $200 adds just 0.2% across $100,000. But for someone already at $96,000 spend it’s worthwhile for the next $4,000. Would I Keep Two $695 American Airlines Cards? I have the regular Citi® / AAdvantage BusinessTM World Elite Mastercard® [See rates and fees], and there’s a reason to spend on it even at one mile per dollar. Through December 31, 2028, eligible purchases on an employee’s card earn a Loyalty Point for the employee and another for the primary cardmember. Both survey designs call that a promotion. On the more interesting version of the premium business card, the extra half Loyalty Point goes to the person whose name is on the card. If employees pay the bills, the owner’s rate on those purchases stays at one. An owner who earns all four personal Executive bonuses from flying could give up 40,000 Loyalty Points by replacing the personal card with that one. The regular business card’s fee goes from $99 to $150 on January 24, 2027. At $100,000 of ordinary spending, E would cost $545 more and earn 50,000 more redeemable miles. That’s 1.09 cents per extra mile before valuing Omni nights or other benefits. If the alternative is a 2% cash back card with no annual fee, though, you’re giving up $2,000 and paying $695. You’d need nearly 1.8 cents apiece from the 150,000 miles to cover both with miles alone. Status remains the reason for spending on the card. A big initial bonus could make either version worth getting for a year. I’d keep my personal Executive and look at replacing my regular business card with this new one. On the more interesting version of the premium business card, the extra half Loyalty Point goes to the person whose name is on the card. If employees pay the bills, the owner’s rate on those purchases stays at one. An owner who earns all four personal Executive bonuses from flying could give up 40,000 Loyalty Points by replacing the personal card with that one. The regular business card’s fee goes from $99 to $150 on January 24, 2027. At $100,000 of ordinary spending, E would cost $545 more and earn 50,000 more redeemable miles. That’s 1.09 cents per extra mile before valuing Omni nights or other benefits. If the alternative is a 2% cash back card with no annual fee, though, you’re giving up $2,000 and paying $695. You’d need nearly 1.8 cents apiece from the 150,000 miles to cover both with miles alone. Status remains the reason for spending on the card. A big initial bonus could make either version worth getting for a year. I’d keep my personal Executive and look at replacing my regular business card with this new one. So you play some primary/AU games. As I was just speculating on DoC, if I’m understanding the proposal correctly, you could get EP without flying by spending $133.33k. And you’d maximize by having the AU do the spending to get EP and then the primary would get PPro with 1x / 133k LP. That’s a significantly better spending for status proposition versus DL/UA. Plus stack with other AA cards (whether a personal Exec, Globe for flight streak, etc.), extra 1x LP on flying with the AA business program, and combine with actual flying… spend for status becomes even cheaper. Almost seems like too good of a deal.

I do think that eventually AA will raise status levels to match the LP accelerator levels with the personal Exec card – so gold will be 60k, plat 100k, ppro 175k and ep 250k. But we will see…

Honestly, Version L combined with the personal Executive Card and the legacy Globe card gets kinda silly at the lower end. Spend $55k and I think you end up with 110k LPs (15k from Globe, then you trip two batches of bonuses).

Serious question. If I always fly business anyway, have a card that gives me lounge access, and purchase tickets using an AX Plat for 5X miles, is there any true inherent marginal value for something like AA Platinum or Platinum Pro (or any other airline high-tier loyalty level?

@Thing 1 – the marginal value in that case is twofold. First, platinum pro gets you oneworld emerald status. Depending on where you are flying, the ability to access first class lounges might be appealing. If you’re a LHR flier, the ability to use the BA First check-in area with private security that leads directly to the BA First lounge, for example – that’s something a business class ticket doesn’t buy you. Want to access Soho when flying out of JFK? Need to be OWE – a business class ticket just gets you Greenwich. You might value that, or may assign that no value.

The other thing that you might value are more miles as a result of being a higher status. So if you’re buying a $5,000 r/t cash business class ticket, you’d get 5x from Amex Plat and another 5x as a general AAdvantage member, but if you were PPro, you’d get 9x, or EP 11x. So that’s an additional 20-30k AA miles, which at 1.5cpm is another $300-450. Maybe that’s something you value, or maybe you’re already getting 50k miles between Amex/AA and getting another 20-30k miles would just be gravy that you don’t need on top of the turkey.

People often ask me about my favorite hotels or my most memorable travel experiences. But because I travel so frequently (and have been doing so for decades), it’s difficult to pick those all-time favorites. I’ll settle for recapping some of my top travel experiences and hotel stays this year.

More so than ever, I’m focusing on experiencing nature — for me, this is really the way to see the world and create lasting memories. Yes, I can fly in all the first-class cabins, but seeing the world's natural wonders and wildlife has been far more life-changing for me.

This year, I also focused on family travel with my kids and parents. My children will be school-age before I know it, so I want to take advantage of not being tied to school holidays to travel and enjoy shoulder-season and offseason escapes when fewer people are traveling.

These were my top hotel stays and travel experiences of 2026.

I’m actually writing this as I return from an epic Norwegian adventure. I was just in Norway with my two sons and my parents, exploring the country in the blustery weather. I started off with a few days in Tromsø, taking my kids to the aquarium (they loved the seals!) and the library. Then, with my family by my side, I saw the northern lights. I’ve seen them before, but admiring them with my children was extra special.

Then we headed out on boat excursions to realize my dream of swimming with orcas, opting to book with Tromsø Pure because they focus on safety and on finding quieter spots away from other boats for a better experience.

At first, we spotted pods of humpbacks, and I was able to swim with them, which was one of the most out-of-body, exhilarating experiences I’ve ever had. There was even a brief moment when I thought I was about to be kicked and/or swallowed by a whale, which was terrifyingly thrilling (don’t worry — I’m still here).

Even though a few of the days had rough seas and low visibility, I was able to swim with orcas later on during the trip, and I’ll never forget it.

After taking nearly a dozen safaris over the years, I was ready for something different. I’ve done the bigger camps and seen the Big 5, so I wanted to try a more niche wildlife experience.

I stayed at Tswalu’s Loapi Lodge in a two-bedroom villa, complete with a plunge pool and my own private chef. I much prefer a lodge to a tented camp, as hearing lions outside your tent at night and having no running water can be a lot to handle, and I’m done roughing it.

Unlike many safari destinations, Tswalu is unique because there aren’t any elephants, but you can see meerkat colonies and observe them relatively up close. I also spotted many black and white rhinos and cheetahs.

I highly recommend Tswalu to experienced safari-goers, but if it’s your first time, I’d suggest going to Cheetah Plains in Sabi Sands or Royal Malewane in Kruger National Park. You’ll get to see the Big 5 and have the perfect introduction to a safari (and you might get addicted to safaris, like I am!).

Many people skip the Caribbean in summer, but honestly, European summer heat can feel even more brutal, with beaches packed umbrella-to-umbrella in places like Spain, Italy and Portugal. This year, I canceled my summer trip to Portugal after a massive heat wave alert and went to Grand Cayman with my kids instead.

Yes, it was warm, but it didn’t feel any hotter than Europe would have (or even a humid Midwest or East Coast summer), and the beach was uncrowded and uncomplicated — no stairs or rugged terrain, like I’ve had to traverse in Portugal. Plus, no jet lag!

My stay at Palm Heights was peaceful, and even though it's a boutique hotel, it felt very family-friendly. I loved that my suite overlooked the white sands of Seven Mile Beach, and the spa was absolutely gorgeous. I highly recommend it for families, couples, or any type of traveler.

In my opinion, the Ritz Paris represents true luxury. I used Chase Points Boost to book it, getting more than 2 cents per point.

The hotel is unapologetically over-the-top, with gorgeous rooms and lavish decor, but what I really love are the service and amenities. The hotel has a program that lets you check in early in the morning after landing from a transatlantic flight, and consumer-friendly options like this are what make it feel truly luxurious. After all, true luxury goes beyond a beautiful room or view — hotels should solve problems, reduce friction, and make traveling easier.

Did you have any special hotel stays or travel experiences this year? Feel free to drop me a comment below and share yours, and be sure to check out our full list for Where to Go in 2027.

I’ve had first hand reports of this as well – the Trump administration has been refusing ESTAs to former U.S. citizens, requiring a full visa, even when they are citizens of and residing in visa waiver countries. The fact alone that they are ex-citizens keeps them from a smooth visit path, independent of any risk factors, and even if they’ve visited using ESTAs for 15 years.

This is a big deal for anyone thinking about renouncing US citizenship.

Many assume they can keep visiting the US after renunciation on ESTA based on their other citizenship. But there are more and more reports of former citizens being denied ESTA and told to apply for a visitor visa instead.

A visitor visa, unlike ESTA, generally requires a consular interview and proving that the applicant will leave after the visit. With family, businesses, or assets in the US, that could mean delays and refusals. This has to factor into the decision on whether or not to renounce.

Southwest Airlines will give you a Companion Pass for a single holiday roundtrip, even if you book the cheapest Basic fare with points. From January 8 through March 3, 2027, you can bring someone on as many trips as you like for just the taxes and fees (from $5.60 each way). You can use points for your seat then, too.

Register for the Black Friday offer first, then book by 11:59 p.m. Central on Sunday, November 29. Put your Rapid Rewards number on the reservation when you book.

Already booked for Christmas? If the same award or paid ticket still costs the same, then register, cancel and rebook. And for a winter trip where you’ll use the pass, you can book your seat now and add your companion once the pass is active, as long as there’s still a seat for sale.

Southwest gets your Christmas booking this weekend and gives you the second seat after the holiday rush. If you earned the pass they offered in August, yours starts January 5 and also ends March 3. This offer adds zero days. You get one designated companion at a time across all your passes, with three changes for 2027 after you pick the first person.

I used to buy my ticket, bring my wife as my companion and redeem points for our daughter. With two kids, I’d register both parents. Each can earn a pass and designate a child. If one parent already earned August’s pass, only the other needs to qualify this time. Fly Austin to Orlando and back nonstop in February and the two kids’ tickets together would cost $22.40 in taxes and fees, even if both parents use points.

This year it takes 135,000 Companion Pass qualifying points or 100 qualifying one-way flights to earn the full pass. Under the Rapid Rewards changes for 2027, unlimited companion travel comes with Platinum status starting January 1. That takes the same 100 flights – or 140,000 tier qualifying points. At 75 flights or 95,000 tier qualifying points you get three companion trips, each of which can be a roundtrip. What made the old pass so easy to earn was that a credit card initial bonus could cover most of those 135,000 points. Next year initial bonuses, referral and anniversary points, extra points from card bonus categories, and points from hotel and rental car partners stop counting toward the pass. A Southwest credit card earns one tier qualifying point per dollar, and cardmembers get a 10,000 point boost when they reach 130,000. Earning the full pass on card spend alone takes $130,000 in purchases. Southwest has also extended the credit card application deadline from December 2 to December 14. Apply by then and get approved, and the 80,000 or 90,000 point initial bonus can count toward the old 135,000 point requirement for a companion pass earned in 2026 even if you finish the required spending in early 2027. Southwest Rapid Rewards® Plus Credit Card (See rates and fees) earn 80,000 bonus points after spending $1,000 on purchases in the first 3 months from account opening. Southwest Rapid Rewards® Priority Credit Card (See rates and fees) earn 90,000 bonus points after spending $3,000 on purchases in the first 3 months from account opening. Any ordinary purchase points you need to close the gap still have to post in 2026. The pass you earn this way runs through December 31, 2027. #6066. Britt bill would launch national office to combat financial fraud

Britt has made fighting elder financial abuse a priority. (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call)

A bill introduced by Sen. Katie Britt on Wednesday aims to combat a rising diversity of financial fraud by unifying the U.S. effort to fight it.

The draft bill would establish a National Office for Scam and Fraud Prevention in the White House that would coordinate federal, state and private sector efforts. It is aimed at ensuring that federal agencies, law enforcement, financial institutions, telecommunications and technology companies and other groups work together, according to an overview from Britt.

The new office would promote intelligence sharing across the public and private sectors, coordinate consumer education efforts and improve assistance for victims.

Britt, R-Ala., said the effort is needed because fraudsters operate nimbly utilizing social media while taking advantage of fragmented or disorganized responses from individual companies and government agencies.

“This effort is about bringing everyone to the table and making sure our response keeps pace with the criminals who are exploiting new technologies and gaps between sectors,” she said in a statement. “When we work together to identify threats earlier and share information more effectively, we can better protect American families and businesses.”

The office would develop a “lexicon of fraud” so that terms for different kinds of scams are standardized between various federal law enforcement agencies to promote a “whole-of-government response,” a Britt aide said.

The office also would work to broaden the approach to combating fraud beyond just having financial institutions reimburse victims. It would tap telecommunications and technology companies to address fraud at its source, such as rip-offs that start as text messages, social media posts or online advertisements.

Britt has made fighting elder financial abuse a priority. She is the sponsor of a bill that would allow state, local and tribal law enforcement agencies to use federal grant funding to investigate financial fraud, particularly scams targeted at the elderly.

The measure highlights the prevalence of "pig butchering," a common technique where a predator cultivates a personal relationship with a victim over many months to extract the most cash.

The House passed its version of the bill in September with overwhelming bipartisan support. The House sponsor is Rep. Zach Nunn, R-Iowa.

Senior financial abuse also was the focus of a bill the House passed in an overwhelming 414-2 vote in June. The legislation, sponsored by Rep. Ann Wagner, R-Mo., would codify Securities and Exchange Commission guidance that permits mutual funds and their agents to postpone the sale of securities if there is a reasonable belief that financial exploitation of someone who is elderly or disabled is occurring

It's not clear whether the Senate will take action on these bills or Britt's by the end of the year.

“If it doesn’t get through in the lame duck, it will continue to be a priority in the 120th [Congress],” the Britt aide said.

But some American Express cardmembers can get $50 back on that same bill at participating hotels if they pay with the enrolled card by December 31, plus Membership Rewards points. CardPointers+ can add the offer to an eligible card and tell you which one to bring. It’s 50% off through Cyber Monday, November 30. A year costs $49.99 (usually $99.99), and lifetime access is $150 (usually $300).

The free version of CardPointers helps you choose a card for groceries or gas. Turn on automatic enrollment in the paid version and the browser extension adds eligible offers when you sign in to American Express, Chase, Bank of America, Citi, Wells Fargo or U.S. Bank. You can search “IHG” before a trip, or the extension can flag a discount while you’re on a store’s website.

On an iPhone, iPad or Mac, you can schedule an overnight check for new offers. If you save your bank logins, your device stores them in its Keychain and signs in directly with the bank. U.S. Bank generally still asks for a verification code each time.

Since August, adding an Amex Offer to one card generally makes it disappear from the others under the same login. CardPointers can pick the card with the highest category bonus (say, Gold for a restaurant offer). You can also give first dibs to a new card where you’re working on an initial bonus.

If I already know to use that Amex at IHG, the app saves me a few clicks. If I’d otherwise pay with my Chase card on a stay I was booking anyway, I’d count the $50 less the value of any extra points I’d earn on Chase. At these prices, lifetime access starts saving money in year four.

#6064. Why Entitlement Reform Is Easier Abroad Than in America

Privatization, among other proposals, requires a particular set of conditions that the U.S. seems to lack.

Pedestrians walk along a street in the Old Town of Stockholm, Sweden, October 17, 2024.

Senator Ron Johnson’s proposal to sustain Social Security payouts even after the projected depletion of its funds in 2032 has attracted new interest in entitlement reform. Fifteen years ago, Paul Ryan became the victim of character assassination over his plans for modest entitlement reforms. In 2005, George W. Bush attempted to reform Social Security, yet his efforts were in vain.

Johnson’s proposal is poorly conceived, even by the low standards of populists. It would set the United States on course to default even faster than it currently is.

John Gustavsson is a writer from Sweden and holds a doctorate in economics. He is Senior Editor of Nation & Citizenship at Restoring the West and a former adviser to the Sweden Democrats in the European Parliament.
